newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banco do Brasil dismisses 500 employees.
newsitem.headline: Banco do Brasil dismisses 500 employees.

text.p: Brazilian government bank Banco do Brasil said it has sacked about 500 excess employees who refused transfers or offers to voluntarily leave the bank.
Banco do Brasil said in a statement it did this after "exhausting all possibilities to reach an agreement with the staff."
Currently, the bank has 84,000 employees, after shedding 13,400 workers via a voluntary redundancy program in 1995.
The dismissals were part of an ongoing restructuring to reduce costs and adapt the bank to increasing competition, the bank said. Since 1995, the bank has posted massive losses.
Like most Brazilian banks, Banco do Brasil suffered from the effects of the elimination of inflation after the implementation of the Real stabilization plan, introduced in July 1994.
By knocking down inflation, the plan also eliminated banks' high earnings on wide spreads.
But, unlike the private banking sector, the bank had made little effort to restructure and survive in a low-inflation environment.
